title: Pagewise - AI Study Assistant
summary: A document Q&A app where you upload PDFs and notes, ask questions, and get answers that cite the exact page they came from.
body:
Pagewise lets you ask questions about your own documents and check every answer. Upload a handbook, a policy, lecture notes or a contract. The app reads the text, splits it into small passages, and stores each one with its page number. When you ask a question, it finds the best passages and sends only those to the AI, which answers from them and cites each one. Ask “How many leave days do I get?” and you get the answer with a numbered citation like “Staff Handbook · page 2”, so you can open the source and confirm it.

**Learning focus:** building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) end to end: document parsing, chunking, search, grounded answers and citations.

**Key features:**

- Upload PDF, TXT or Markdown files up to 4 MB
- Text split into passages that keep their page numbers
- Search by meaning and by keyword _(verify: hybrid search)_
- Answers come only from your documents, with a numbered citation on every claim
- Citations show the document name and page
- Accounts, so each person sees only their own documents _(verify)_
- Demo login for a quick try
- Dark, minimal design

**What I learned:**

- Parsing PDFs and splitting text into chunks without losing page numbers
- Searching by meaning (embeddings) and by keyword, then combining the results _(verify)_
- Writing prompts that make the AI answer only from the supplied passages
- Making the AI cite its sources, and checking those citations against the passages that were actually retrieved _(verify)_
- Telling the user when the documents don’t contain the answer, instead of guessin
